text:
alice: Heads-up — seeing a sharp throughput drop on dedicated cluster arnold around 09:12 UTC. 99th p50 token latency jumped, queues backed up, customers reporting slow responses. Anyone watching autoscale/events?

ben: Looking now. Can you paste the job/id or customer id? link to grafana? :thinking:

alice: customer_id=acct-17f, job=dedicated/arnold/pool-3. grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/teams/eng-runtime/dedicated_throughput?panelId=12 — QPS down ~60% vs baseline.

carol: support saw multiple 503/rate_limited for acct-17f and some 504 timeouts. Customer sent curl repro: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":512}'` — got `{"error":"server_busy"}` repeatedly.

dave: grabbing scheduler/autoscaler logs. infra-bot: autoscaler event at 09:13: scale_down prevented (concurrent floater).

infra-bot: [event] 2026-03-17T09:13:11Z autoscaler: suppress_scale_down due to pending_rebalance=1; pool=pool-3; avail_gpus=6

ben: If autoscaler was suppressed we might be dealing with noisy tenant or batcher inefficiency starving throughput. Any batcher logs?

alice: Attached minimal log snippet from runtime (trimmed):
```
I0317 09:12:58 scheduler.cpp:214] batcher.window_ms=12
I0317 09:12:58 batcher.cpp:382] max_batch_tokens=256 current_tokens_inflight=48 avg_seq_len=32
I0317 09:13:05 batcher.cpp:410] forming batch: n_reqs=3 tokens=96 (3 small requests)
I0317 09:13:18 kvcache.cpp:122] cache_hit_rate=0.03
I0317 09:13:45 scheduler.cpp:300] queue_depth=148 wakeups=320
```
\ncarol: cache hit rate super low — might be varied prompts from this tenant causing small batches.

dave: That log shows lots of small groups forming (n_reqs=3). Combined with conservative max_batch_tokens=256 we end up sending many underutilized micro-batches. If these are arriving as short sequences it's hurting throughput. Also autoscaler suppression means we didn't quickly add capacity.

ben: Repro checklist for support/SRE:
- reproduce with customer traffic pattern (short prompts bursty).
- simulate with loadtool: `wrk -t8 -c200 --script short_prompt.lua https://dedicated.arnold.redwood/pool-3`
- collect `/var/log/redwood/batcher.log` + scheduler metrics + per-GPU utilization.

alice: Running a quick local repro with wrk now, already see avg batch size=2.1 and GPU util ~32%.

dave: Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) increase `max_batch_tokens` from 256 -> 1024 (non-disruptive config flip on pool) to allow larger aggregate batches for short-seq traffic.
2) temporarily relax `min_batch_fill_ms` from 12 -> 40 to give the batcher a slightly longer window to accumulate requests.
3) if that doesn't help, enable short-term burst pool (if available) to add 2 nodes.

carol: From support side I'll notify acct-17f that we're investigating and ask for a short replay window (09:05-09:25) and any client-side rate throttles.

ben: Quick safety checks before config change: make sure other tenants on pool-3 won't see increased p99 due to larger batching windows (risk: longer tail for single-request latency). Can we try config on a canary insert first?

dave: Yes. Plan: canary on pool-3-node-7 (10:00 UTC), flip `max_batch_tokens` to 1024 + `min_batch_fill_ms`=30. Watch QPS, avg batch size, p50/p95 latency, GPU util. If metrics look good for 10m, roll to remaining nodes.

alice: Can I get a quick patch command for the runtime?

dave: Patch via ops-runner: `ops-runner apply-config --pool pool-3 --node pool-3-node-7 --set batcher.max_batch_tokens=1024,batcher.min_batch_fill_ms=30`

ben: Also open an incident ticket and tag oncall: #INC-18425, assign to dave. I'll be the liaison.

infra-bot: [ticket created] INC-18425 — Dedicated throughput drop / batching inefficiency (assigned dave).

carol: Noted — customer updated. :white_check_mark:

alice: After canary flip (09:22 UTC) I see avg batch size jump to 11.8 and GPU util -> 78%. QPS recovered ~55%. p95 latency improved from 1.8s -> 0.9s.

dave: Good sign. Keep canary for 15 min, then rollout. Also creating follow-up to add adaptive max_batch_tokens tuning based on observed avg_seq_len histogram.

ben: Action items:
- dave: roll canary to pool after 10m if stable, file PR for scheduler adaptive tuning RFC.
- carol: collect customer replay and confirm resolution.
- alice: attach perf graphs to INC-18425.

alice: Done — graphs attached, marking as working on rolling. :rocket:

dave: Rolling change at 09:40 UTC. Roll complete 09:47 UTC. No regressions seen.

ben: Closing incident after 1h verify window if no regressions. Great work team. :clap:

carol: Customer confirmed response times back to normal and happy to accept post-mortem.

alice: Filing short postmortem summary and scheduler tuning RFC. Will include repro script and canary run notes.

ben: thumbs-up.

(emoji reactions: :rocket: :white_check_mark: :clap: on various posts)
